pages.title: Grit-singers
text: “The mesh does not find the ore. The mesh gives the ore somewhere to land.”

pages.title: Who they are
text: The Grit-singers sang low over raw stone until it loosened, and lower still until it shattered into echo. Their craft is **the Echo Shatter and the meshes**.
Their camps stand in **mountains** and on stony shores, and a second camp keeps the old road in the March highlands.

pages.title: What they want
text: Their reagent is the **Attuned Echo**, worth **+8** standing at their hearth.
They also favour raw ores, ore blocks, Iron Grit, Gold Grit or Copper Grit: **+3** each. Any other food is worth **+1**, and a charged Pulse Cell **+2 for every 10 Pulse**, up to +8.
Remember the hearth takes at most **60** standing a day from offerings; see [Tribes and standing](standing).

pages.title: What the Elder trades
text: **Guest**: 4 Raw Iron for 3 Echo Shards; 4 Attuned Echo and 8 March Stone for a Resonance Mesh.
**Friend**: 6 Iron Grit for 2 Attuned Echo; 3 Raw Gold for 4 Gold Grit.
**Kin**: 6 Attuned Echo for 2 Bound Echo; 4 Bound Echo for an Echo Shatter.

pages.title: Their Mark and totem
text: At **Voice** the Elder gives you the Grit-singers' Tribe Mark. Craft it with a {item:tribalpower:resonance_totem_earth} and two Spiritweave into their [Kinship Totem](kinship_totem).
Beside a Pulse Resonator it is one more voice; beside a station it lends **Earth**.

Your standing with the Grit-singers decides how deep a [Listening Pit](listening_pit) may listen: **Friend** for common ore, **Kin** for the deep and hot bands, **Voice** for the rare one. Their Kinship Totem is one of the two ways to open the deeper bands.
